question: What metal is most commonly used to manufacture standard surgical instruments?
explanation: Stainless steel is chosen because it resists rust and can survive the high temperatures of repeated sterilization cycles. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why must a scrub nurse know the exact name and purpose of every surgical instrument?

options.A: It is a legal requirement for writing the patient's record
options.B: It helps the doctor finish the operation without speaking
options.C: It prevents prolonged surgery and accidental tissue damage
options.D: It stops the instruments from rusting during the procedure

explanation: Knowing your tools allows you to anticipate the surgeon's needs quickly, keeping the operation safe and efficient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of clamping and occluding instruments?

options.A: To compress blood vessels and stop bleeding
options.B: To hold wound edges open for better visibility
options.C: To cut through tough bone and cartilage
options.D: To stitch the skin closed at the end of surgery

explanation: Clamping tools like hemostats squeeze bleeding vessels shut to maintain a clear field of vision during the procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why are surgical instruments divided into functional categories?

options.A: To keep the trolley organized and speed up instrument passing
options.B: To make it easier for the manufacturer to price them
options.C: To prevent the hospital from losing small metal pieces
options.D: To ensure every tray contains the exact same number of items

explanation: Categorizing instruments helps the nurse keep the sterile field orderly and respond instantly to the surgeon's requests. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which scissors are best suited for cutting delicate, fine tissues?
explanation: Metzenbaum scissors have fine, slender tips specifically designed for careful dissection of delicate internal tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why should a nurse avoid using heavy Mayo scissors to cut fine sutures or delicate tissue?

options.A: It blunts the blades and ruins the precision of the tool
options.B: It makes the instrument too hot to handle safely
options.C: It causes the surgical lights to flicker and lose focus
options.D: It violates standard hospital waste disposal rules

explanation: Using heavy instruments on delicate items damages the cutting edge, making future dissections difficult and traumatic for the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which type of grasping instrument is safest to use on delicate organs like the bowel?
explanation: Smooth forceps lack sharp teeth, preventing them from puncturing or tearing fragile internal organs during manipulation. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: A surgeon asks for a forceps to securely hold tough skin edges during wound closure. Which instrument should you hand over?
explanation: Toothed forceps grip tough structures like skin firmly without slipping, making them ideal for closing surface wounds. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a hemostat in the operating theatre?

options.A: To cut through thick muscle and bone
options.B: To compress bleeding vessels and stop bleeding
options.C: Holding surgical drapes to the skin
options.D: Incision of the outer skin layer

explanation: Hemostats squeeze bleeding blood vessels shut so the surgical team can control hemorrhage and keep the field clean. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why do surgeons often prefer curved hemostats over straight ones when tying off blood vessels?

options.A: They prevent the instrument from locking accidentally
options.B: Curved handles are much easier to open with one hand
options.C: The curve improves visibility around the tip for placing a tie
options.D: Straight hemostats are only used for cutting thread

explanation: The curved jaw allows the surgeon to see the vessel tip clearly and pass suture material around it safely. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of a self-retaining retractor like the Weitlaner?

options.A: It locks open automatically, freeing up assistant hands
options.B: It has a built-in light source to illuminate deep wounds
options.C: It does not require any sterilization between cases
options.D: It can also be used as a cutting instrument for bone

explanation: Self-retaining retractors use a ratchet lock to stay open on their own, reducing fatigue for the surgical team. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why should a nurse remind the team to periodically release a retractor during a long operation?

options.A: To allow the metal joints to cool down from body heat
options.B: To clean off accumulated blood and keep the instrument shiny
options.C: To prevent tissue damage and lack of blood supply from constant pressure
options.D: To change the size of the wound opening as the surgery progresses

explanation: Continuous heavy retraction can cut off blood flow to the edges of the wound, leading to localized tissue death. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: Where should the surgical needle be grasped by the needle holder?

options.A: At the extreme tail end of the thread
options.B: One-third to one-half from the swaged end
options.C: Right at the very sharp point of the needle
options.D: Directly in the exact middle of the curve

explanation: Holding the needle at this position gives the best balance of control and prevents the needle from bending or breaking. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a needle holder during wound closure?

options.A: To clamp bleeding blood vessels in the subcutaneous fat
options.B: To pull back skin edges for a better view of the muscle
options.C: To cut excess suture thread after the knot is tied
options.D: To firmly grip the needle and drive it through tissue safely

explanation: Needle holders provide a strong, stable grip so the surgeon can guide the needle through tough layers without slipping. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why must instrument box locks and ratchets be kept open during the sterilization process?

options.A: To make it easier to count them after the cycle
options.B: To allow steam to reach all hidden surfaces
options.C: To make the instrument tray look neat and tidy
options.D: To prevent the metal handles from melting

explanation: Keeping hinges and box locks open ensures that the sterilizing steam makes full contact with every part of the metal. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)

question: What should the nurse do immediately upon discovering a cracked jaw on a hemostat during preparation?

options.A: Return it to the standard surgical tray without telling anyone
options.B: Remove the instrument from service and report the damage
options.C: Apply strong glue to the crack before sending it to autoclave
options.D: Use it only for minor tasks away from deep organs

explanation: Damaged instruments must be taken out of circulation immediately to prevent pieces from breaking off inside a patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)
